Chapter 6: Rebuilding Trust—With Yourself and Others
After the initial shock fades, and you’ve taken those first steps to protect yourself, there’s a question that naturally comes up: How do you ever trust again?
Trust, once it’s been broken, can feel a bit like a vase that’s been shattered—sure, you can try to glue it back together, but will it ever look or feel the same?
Here’s the good news: with some patience and intention, you can create a new sense of trust—both in yourself, and if you want, with others.
Let’s start with the first layer: rebuilding trust in yourself.
Betrayal can really make you doubt your own judgment. You might find yourself replaying old decisions, second-guessing your instincts, or wondering if you’ll ever be able to spot the truth again.
But here’s something to remember—your intuition and discernment aren’t lost forever. They’re skills, and just like any skill, they can be rebuilt and strengthened over time.
So, how do you do that? Well, it helps to look back at moments when your gut feeling was right, even if you didn’t act on it then. Try making small, low-pressure choices and really honoring them.
And if you catch yourself sliding into self-blame, pause and practice a little self-compassion instead. It’s not about being perfect—it’s about being kind to yourself during the process.
Now, what about trusting others? Whether it’s a partner hoping to make things right, or new people stepping into your life, trust isn’t something you can just flip on like a light switch.
Think of it more like building a bridge, one plank at a time.
What does that look like in real life? It means setting clear expectations for honesty and transparency, and watching to see if words and actions actually line up over time.
Let trust grow at its own pace—don’t force forgiveness or rush into closeness before you’re ready.
Here’s a metaphor I love: trust is like a garden. It needs regular care, patience, and sometimes, you’ll have to pull out the weeds of doubt when they pop up.
If you decide to stay in a relationship after betrayal, rebuilding trust might include open communication exercises, setting shared goals, or even trying couples counseling together.
And if you choose to move on, these same principles still apply. With new connections, start small, pay attention to what you’re feeling, and honor the boundaries that keep you safe.
So, whether you’re learning to trust yourself again or opening up to others, remember—it’s okay to take it slow. Each step, no matter how small, is a step toward healing.
